mainTopic: Purification of a בעל קרי after תקנת עזרא, and keeping תפלה and קריאת שמע clean of impurity and filth
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: רב אסי rules that a חולה whose emission was involuntary is fully exempt, and רב יוסף says this makes רב נחמן's nine-קבין jug useful again. The גמרא then asks what עזרא actually enacted. אביי credits עזרא with both ארבעים סאה and תשעה קבין. רבא rejects this and explains that עזרא enacted only טבילה, and later רבנן added the nine קבין. רבא then gives the practical הלכה for all four cases of healthy or sick, regular or involuntary. A ברייתא distinguishes purity for one's own learning from purity for teaching others, and the אמוראים argue over how to read it. The story of three אמוראים competing to lead ברכת המזון applies this distinction, but the הלכה does not follow רב חמא's practice of immersing to act for others. A new משנה follows about a בעל קרי who remembers his status during תפלה, saying קריאת שמע while immersing, and keeping four אמות from filth. The גמרא then discusses צואה seen or found during תפלה, and urine flowing during תפלה. That last discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אסי rules that a sick person with an involuntary emission is fully exempt
steps.stepSummary: In רב אושעיא's chamber the question was brought to רב אסי. He answered that the requirement of pouring water applies only to a חולה המרגיל, while a חולה לאונסו is פטור מכלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the chamber of רב אושעיא they came and asked רב אסי. He told them: the rule was taught only about a sick person who had a normal emission. A sick person who had an involuntary emission is exempt from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began on the previous amud: a question came up in רב אושעיא's study hall and was brought to רב אסי. He answers by limiting the earlier teaching about pouring water on a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching said a חולה needs תשעה קבין poured on him. רב אסי says that teaching was only about a חולה המרגיל, meaning a normal emission. A חולה לאונסו needs no water at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... (limits a rule to a narrower case)
A sick person who had a normal emission (from ordinary relations or desire)
Involuntary, not caused by his own desire
Exempt from anything, so no water is needed at all

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'sick versus healthy' with 'normal versus involuntary'. These are two separate distinctions, and together they make four different cases.

phrases.english: In the chamber of Rav Oshaya,
they came and asked Rav Asi.
He said to them: They only taught it
regarding a sick person who had a normal emission,
but a sick person who had an involuntary emission
is exempt from anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ וּשְׁאִלוּ לְרַב אַסִּי. אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion on the previous amud about the teaching on a sick בעל קרי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the requirement of תשעה קבין for a חולה also covers an involuntary emission.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Only a חולה המרגיל needs it, and a חולה לאונסו is exempt from everything.

steps.title: רב יוסף says רב נחמן's jug is restored
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reacts to רב אסי's ruling. רב נחמן's jug of תשעה קבין, which he had earlier called 'broken', is now 'rejoined' and useful again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב נחמן's jug has been put back together.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף makes a colorful comment about what רב אסי's ruling means. רב נחמן used a jug holding nine קבין, and that practice is now valid again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב יוסף had said the jug was 'broken', meaning רב נחמן's practice seemed refuted. רב אסי now limits the nine-קבין teaching to a חולה המרגיל, while a חולה לאונסו is fully exempt. So a real case is again left for nine קבין, a sick person with a normal emission, and the jug has a use again.

keyTerms.meaning: Was rejoined or reattached, so it is whole again
An earthenware jug (here, רב נחמן's jug holding nine קבין)
An אמורא who kept a nine-קב jug for purification

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rav Nachman's jug has been rejoined.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִצְטְמִיד חַצְבֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of רב אסי's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of רב אסי's ruling, רב נחמן's practice of using nine קבין is valid again.

steps.title: Let us see how עזרא originally set up his תקנה
steps.stepSummary: Since all the תנאים and אמוראים are really arguing about the scope of תקנת עזרא, the גמרא proposes to work out what עזרא actually enacted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since all the אמוראים and תנאים are arguing about עזרא's enactment, let us look at how עזרא set it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back from the individual opinions and asks a big-picture question. This step sets up the next move, where אביי and then רבא each describe עזרא's original enactment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the opinions so far differ on how far the requirement for a בעל קרי reaches. The גמרא suggests that if we understand exactly what עזרא enacted, every opinion can be mapped onto it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all (opens a logical observation)
עזרא the Scribe, who enacted that a בעל קרי must immerse

phrases.english: Since all the Amoraim and Tannaim
are disagreeing about Ezra's enactment,
let us see how Ezra enacted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי כּוּלְּהוּ אָמוֹרָאֵי וְתַנָּאֵי בִּדְעֶזְרָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from individual rulings to the source that all of them depend on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly עזרא enacted for a בעל קרי.

steps.title: אביי says עזרא enacted both ארבעים סאה and תשעה קבין
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, עזרא enacted ארבעים סאה for a בריא המרגיל and תשעה קבין for a בריא לאונסו. The אמוראים later argued only about a חולה, and אביי lays out their two positions.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: עזרא enacted forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission, and nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission. Then the אמוראים came and argued about a sick person. One said a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission, and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission. The other said a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission, and a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. In his view, עזרא himself set two levels for healthy people, and the later argument is only about sick people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion maps the sick cases directly onto the healthy ones. The second opinion moves each sick case down one level: a normal emission needs only nine קבין, and an involuntary one needs nothing. The key claim here, which רבא will challenge, is that עזרא himself enacted the nine קבין.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty סאה, the minimum size of a מקוה for full immersion
Nine קבין of water poured over the person
One master holds... and the other master holds

phrases.english: Abaye said: Ezra enacted
for a healthy person with a normal emission, forty se'ah,
and for a healthy person with an involuntary emission, nine kav.
And the Amoraim came and disagreed about a sick person.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר חוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל
phrases.english: One master holds: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission,
and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר חוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא לְאוֹנְסוֹ,
phrases.english: And the other master holds: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission,
and a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: עֶזְרָא תַּקֵּן לְבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how עזרא enacted.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עזרא enacted two levels, ארבעים סאה and תשעה קבין, and the argument about a חולה came later.

steps.title: רבא objects that עזרא never enacted pouring
steps.stepSummary: רבא attacks אביי's claim. The tradition says עזרא enacted only טבילה for בעלי קריין, so how could the pouring of nine קבין (נתינה) be part of תקנת עזרא?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Fine, עזרא enacted immersion, but did he enact pouring?! The master said that עזרא enacted immersion for those who had an emission!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's version of history. He points to a known tradition that says עזרא's enactment was only about immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי attributed the nine קבין, which are poured, to עזרא himself. But the received wording is 'עזרא תיקן טבילה', which mentions immersion only. So pouring cannot be part of עזרא's original enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: People who had a seminal emission
But did the master not say...? (brings a known source as a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: נְהִי דְּתַקֵּן עֶזְרָא טְבִילָה,
phrases.english: Rava said: Granted that Ezra enacted immersion,
did he enact pouring?!
But didn't the master say:
Ezra enacted immersion for those who had an emission.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּתַקֵּן עֶזְרָא טְבִילָה, נְתִינָה מִי תַּקֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that עזרא enacted תשעה קבין for a בריא לאונסו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tradition says עזרא enacted טבילה only, so נתינה cannot be part of his enactment.

steps.title: רבא rebuilds the history in three layers
steps.stepSummary: רבא's reconstruction has three layers. עזרא enacted only טבילה in ארבעים סאה for a בריא המרגיל. Later רבנן added תשעה קבין for a בריא לאונסו. Later still the אמוראים argued about a חולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: עזרא enacted immersion in forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission. Then the רבנן came and enacted nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission. Then the אמוראים came and argued about a sick person. One said a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission, and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission. The other said a healthy person with a normal emission needs forty סאה, a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission and needs nine קבין, but a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own account of the history to avoid his own challenge. The nine קבין is no longer credited to עזרא. It is a later rabbinic addition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from אביי is who enacted the nine קבין. Now it comes from later רבנן, which fits the tradition that עזרא enacted only immersion. The argument about a חולה stays the same as in אביי's version.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier version and offers a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three layers. עזרא enacted ארבעים סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission. Later רבנן enacted תשעה קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission. The אמוראים then argued whether a חולה is treated the same as a healthy person, or one level lighter, with a חולה לאונסו fully exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: Separating what עזרא enacted from what later רבנן added explains why there are different water amounts and why the rules for a חולה can be lenient.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Ezra enacted immersion
for a healthy person with a normal emission, in forty se'ah.
And the Rabbis came and enacted
for a healthy person with an involuntary emission, nine kav.
And the Amoraim came and disagreed about a sick person:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר חוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל,
phrases.english: One master holds: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission,
and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission;

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר לְבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה,
phrases.english: and the other master holds: a healthy person with a normal emission needs forty se'ah,

phrases.aramaic: וְחוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא לְאוֹנְסוֹ — תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין.
phrases.english: and a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission, needing nine kav.
But a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: עֶזְרָא תַּקֵּן טְבִילָה לְבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own challenge by replacing אביי's account.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical reattribution: the nine קבין is credited to later רבנן instead of to עזרא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to אביי, עזרא himself enacted both ארבעים סאה and תשעה קבין.
steps.terutzMaskana: עזרא enacted only טבילה. Later רבנן added נתינה of תשעה קבין, and the אמוראים argued about a חולה.

steps.title: רבא's practical ruling for all four cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules: a healthy or sick person who is מרגיל needs forty סאה. A healthy person לאונסו needs nine קבין. A sick person לאונסו is completely exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said the הלכה is this. A healthy person or a sick person whose emission was the regular kind needs forty סאה. A healthy person whose emission was accidental needs nine קבין. A sick person whose emission was accidental is exempt from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the reconstructions of תקנת עזרא, רבא now gives the bottom-line הלכה. It covers every combination of healthy or sick, and regular or accidental.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four cases, sorted by two questions: was the person healthy or sick, and was the emission regular or accidental? The more 'normal' the emission, the stricter the requirement. The most lenient case, a חולה לאונסו, needs nothing at all. For a חולה המרגיל, רבא is strict and treats him exactly like a healthy person: forty סאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה, the final ruling
A healthy person whose emission was the regular kind, for example through marital relations
A sick person whose emission was accidental
Exempt from everything, so no washing or immersion is needed

steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: מרגיל, whether healthy or sick, needs forty סאה. בריא לאונסו needs nine קבין. חולה לאונסו needs nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the debate over the scope of תקנת עזרא with a clear practical chart for all four cases.

phrases.english: Rava said: the halakha is:
a healthy person with a regular emission and a sick person with a regular emission
need forty se'a.
And a healthy person with an accidental emission needs nine kav.
But a sick person with an accidental emission is exempt from everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after רבא's three-layer reconstruction of the תקנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Regular emission, healthy or sick: forty סאה. Healthy and accidental: nine קבין. Sick and accidental: exempt.

steps.title: A ברייתא on nine קבין for oneself and forty סאה for others
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that nine קבין poured over a בעל קרי make him pure for his own learning. Teaching others needs forty סאה. רבי יהודה requires forty סאה in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a בעל קרי who had nine קבין of water poured on him is pure. When is that true? Only for himself. But for others he needs forty סאה. רבי יהודה says forty סאה are needed in all cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, that adds a fresh distinction. It matters whether the person wants to learn for himself or teach others. This sets up the next argument among the אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא adds a new factor: who the learning is for. Nine קבין is enough for one's own learning, but teaching others needs the stricter forty סאה. רבי יהודה disagrees and makes no such split, so forty סאה are always required.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission
In what case was this said? It introduces a limit on the rule just stated
For himself, meaning his own learning
For others, meaning teaching Torah to others
In any case, with no distinctions

steps.confusionAlert: Nine קבין and forty סאה are not just two amounts of water. Nine קבין are poured over the person (נתינה), while forty סאה is an immersion (טבילה).

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A man who had an emission, over whom they poured
nine kav of water, is pure.
When is this said? For himself,
but for others he needs forty se'a.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: forty se'a in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא that adds a new distinction: learning for oneself versus teaching others
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: nine קבין are enough for oneself, forty סאה for teaching others. רבי יהודה: forty סאה always.

steps.title: Does the forty סאה for teaching others also apply to a sick person whose emission was accidental?
steps.stepSummary: Four אמוראים form two pairs. One member from each pair argues about the first clause. One says the 'forty סאה for others' rule applies only to a חולה המרגיל, so a חולה לאונסו needs only nine קבין. The other says anyone teaching others needs forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were four אמוראים: רבי יוחנן, רבי יהושע בן לוי, רבי אלעזר, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. One from each pair argued about the first part of the ברייתא. One said: when you said 'for himself nine קבין, but for others forty סאה,' that was taught only about a sick person whose emission was regular. A sick person whose emission was accidental needs only nine קבין. The other said: anyone teaching others, even a sick person whose emission was accidental, needs forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a מחלוקת about how to read the first clause of the ברייתא. It first names the four אמוראים, arranged in two pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view narrows the 'forty סאה for others' rule to a חולה המרגיל. In his view, a חולה לאונסו stays at nine קבין even for teaching. The second view says teaching others always needs forty סאה, no matter the person's condition. We are not told which אמורא held which view.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about, which limits the rule's scope

steps.confusionAlert: The text does not say which of the four אמוראים held which view. It only says that one person from each pair argued here.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

phrases.aramaic: חַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: One of this pair and one of that pair argued on the first clause.
One said: That which you said,
'When is this said? For himself,
but for others forty se'a,'
was taught only about a sick person with a regular emission,
but for a sick person with an accidental emission, nine kav.
And one said: anyone teaching others,
even a sick person with an accidental emission,
is not pure until there are forty se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues about how to read the first clause of the ברייתא in Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: View 1: forty סאה for others applies only to a חולה המרגיל, so a חולה לאונסו needs nine קבין. View 2: teaching others always needs forty סאה.

steps.title: Must רבי יהודה's forty סאה be in the ground, or can they be in vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The other member of each pair argues about the second clause. One says רבי יהודה's forty סאה must be water in the ground. The other says forty סאה collected in vessels also work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one from this pair and one from that pair argued about the end of the ברייתא. One said: when רבי יהודה said 'forty סאה in any case,' that was taught only about water in the ground, not in vessels. The other said: even in vessels it works.
steps.whatsHappening: The other two אמוראים argue about רבי יהודה's view in the second clause of the ברייתא. The question is what kind of forty סאה he requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view requires a real מקוה-type gathering of water in the ground. The second view says this is only a rabbinic purification, so forty סאה gathered in vessels are also acceptable. The argument is about the quality of the water, not its amount.

keyTerms.meaning: In the ground, like a proper מקוה
In vessels, meaning water collected in containers

steps.whatToRemember: Two מחלוקות on the ברייתא. First clause: does a חולה לאונסו need forty סאה to teach others? Second clause: can רבי יהודה's forty סאה be in vessels?

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַסֵּיפָא.
phrases.english: And one of this pair and one of that pair argued on the latter clause.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הָא דְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: One said: That which Rabbi Yehuda said,
'forty se'a in any case,'
was taught only about water in the ground,
but in vessels, no.
And one said: even in vessels as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The matching argument on the second clause, by the other member of each pair
steps.mimraCoreRuling: View 1: רבי יהודה's forty סאה must be in the ground. View 2: forty סאה in vessels are also acceptable.

steps.title: What does 'in any case' add for the 'only in the ground' view?
steps.stepSummary: The 'vessels also work' reading explains רבי יהודה's phrase מכל מקום well. The גמרא asks what that phrase includes for the 'only in the ground' reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says that forty סאה works even in vessels. That is why רבי יהודה says 'forty סאה in any case.' But the other opinion says water in the ground works and water in vessels does not. For that opinion, what does 'in any case' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the opinion from Step 10 that רבי יהודה's forty סאה must be water in the ground. It asks how that opinion explains the words 'מכל מקום'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In any case' sounds like it includes everything, even water held in vessels. That fits the opinion that vessels also work. For the 'ground only' opinion, the phrase seems to have nothing left to include. So the גמרא asks what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (according to one view)
In any case / in every situation
The ground (water gathered naturally in the earth)
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said even in vessels,
that is why it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מִכׇּל מָקוֹם״.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: 'Forty se'a in any case.'
But according to the one who said in the ground, yes,
phrases.notes: This is the 'ground only' opinion from Step 10.

phrases.english: in vessels, no,
what does 'in any case' come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֲפִילּוּ בְּכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the 'ground only' reading from Step 10 against the wording of the ברייתא from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that רבי יהודה's forty סאה must be water in the ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word מכל מקום seems to include vessels. If vessels are excluded, the phrase appears to add nothing.

steps.title: It includes drawn water
steps.stepSummary: 'In any case' includes מים שאובין, water drawn by people and poured into a pool in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include drawn water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 11. Even on the 'ground only' view, 'in any case' includes water that people drew and then collected in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מקוה may not be filled with drawn water. For a בעל קרי, though, רבי יהודה is lenient. Forty סאה in the ground works even if people drew and poured it there. That is the leniency the phrase 'in any case' adds, so vessels do not need to be included.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawn water, carried or poured by human hand (normally not valid for a מקוה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'drawn water' with 'water in vessels.' Here the water sits in the ground, but people brought it there. That is allowed. Water that is still inside a container is what the 'ground only' opinion rejects.

phrases.english: To include drawn water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוּיֵי מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the phrase a different meaning, so it no longer needs to include vessels.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In any case' seemed to mean 'even in vessels.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In any case' means 'even drawn water collected in the ground.'

steps.title: רב פפא offers to lead ברכת המזון after nine קבין
steps.stepSummary: Three אמוראים ate together. רב פפא asked to lead ברכת המזון because nine קבין of water had been poured on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, רב הונא the son of רב יהושע, and רבא ברבי בר שמואל ate bread together. רב פפא said to them: 'Let me lead the ברכה, because nine קבין have fallen on me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that applies the rules about purification from קרי. רב פפא makes the first claim to lead ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leading ברכת המזון means saying the ברכה on behalf of others. רב פפא thinks the nine קבין poured on him are enough. In the next step this claim will be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me lead the blessing (ברכת המזון)
For it has fallen upon me

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
and Rava b'Rabbi bar Shmuel
ate bread together.
Rav Pappa said to them:
Let me be the one to bless,
for nine kav have fallen upon me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרָבָא בְּרַבִּי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרִיכוּ רִיפְתָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the textual discussion to a practical story about the same rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא held that nine קבין qualified him to lead others in ברכת המזון.

steps.title: רבא ברבי בר שמואל: for others you need forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: רבא ברבי בר שמואל quotes the ברייתא: nine קבין work only for oneself, and acting for others needs forty סאה. He had immersed in forty סאה, so he claims the right to lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא ברבי בר שמואל said to them: 'We learned: when does this rule apply? For himself. But for others he needs forty סאה. Rather, let me lead the ברכה, because forty סאה have fallen on me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא ברבי בר שמואל rejects רב פפא's claim using the ברייתא from Step 8. He offers himself instead, since he immersed in forty סאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said nine קבין are enough for learning by yourself, and teaching others needs forty סאה. רבא ברבי בר שמואל treats leading ברכת המזון for a group like teaching others. So nine קבין are not enough for that.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (limits a rule)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא בְּרַבִּי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rava b'Rabbi bar Shmuel said to them:
We learned: in what case was this said? For himself,
but for others, forty se'a.
Rather, let me be the one to bless,
for forty se'a have fallen upon me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא בְּרַבִּי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּנֵינָא, בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's claim from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that nine קבין qualify him to lead others.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits nine קבין to acting for oneself, and leading a group counts as acting for others.

steps.title: רב הונא: I never needed either
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא claims the right to lead because he was never a בעל קרי, so he needed neither nine קבין nor forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to them: 'Let me lead the ברכה, because neither this nor that is upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא makes the final and strongest claim. He was fully pure and never needed any purification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each speaker claims a higher level of purity. Nine קבין is the lowest, forty סאה is next, and never having become impure is the highest. רב הונא's claim tops both earlier ones, since someone who was never impure needs no purification at all. The גמרא does not say who actually led the ברכה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to them:
Let me be the one to bless,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלֵיכָּא עִילָּוַאי לָא הַאי וְלָא הַאי.
phrases.english: for there is upon me neither this nor that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא: הַבוּ לִי לְדִידִי לִבְרוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond both earlier claims with a higher level of purity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who was never impure is clearly fit to lead others.

steps.title: רב חמא immersed on ערב פסח for the public
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא used to immerse on ערב פסח so he could help the public fulfill their obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא would immerse on the eve of פסח in order to fulfill the obligations of the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports another practice that follows the 'for others needs more' idea. Its ruling on this practice comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חמא held, like the ברייתא, that acting on behalf of others requires full immersion. He immersed before פסח because he would be leading the public, for example in the ברכות of the night.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill the obligation of the many on their behalf

phrases.english: Rav Hama would immerse
on the eve of Passover
in order to fulfill the obligation of the many.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חָמָא טָבֵיל בְּמַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְפִסְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practice based on the 'for others' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חמא required immersion before acting on behalf of the public.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רב חמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules against רב חמא's practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the section with a practical ruling. We do not follow רב חמא's practice of immersing before acting for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא rejects the idea that someone needs special immersion to act for others. Many explain this as part of the broader trend that immersion for a בעל קרי is no longer practiced.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: Step 12: according to the 'ground only' view, 'מכל מקום' includes מים שאובין. In the story, the levels go from nine קבין, to forty סאה, to never being impure, and each speaker's claim to lead is stronger than the one before. In practice, the הלכה does not require special immersion in order to lead others, as רב חמא did.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line. In practice, a בעל קרי does not need special immersion before leading others in a ברכה or a מצוה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is not in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on רב חמא's practice from Step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Special immersion in order to act on behalf of others is not required in practice.

steps.title: משנה: Remembering in the middle of תפלה that one is impure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who remembers during תפלה that he is a בעל קרי should not stop. He should shorten his prayer instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone was standing in prayer and remembered that he had a seminal emission, he should not stop. Rather, he should shorten his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the first rule: a בעל קרי who is already in the middle of תפלה finishes in a shortened form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא discussed the enactment that a בעל קרי should not say holy words until he immerses. This משנה deals with someone who has already started. He does not stop completely, but he also does not say the full long version. He cuts each ברכה short.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
A man who had a seminal emission and has not yet immersed
He should not stop or interrupt

steps.confusionAlert: 'יקצר' does not mean he skips the תפלה. He keeps going but says a short version of each ברכה.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If one was standing in prayer
and remembered that he had a seminal emission,
he should not stop, but rather shorten.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of immersion for a בעל קרי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי who remembers his status mid-תפלה does not stop; he shortens.

steps.title: משנה: Immersing and saying קריאת שמע before sunrise
steps.stepSummary: A person who went to immerse should come up, get dressed, and say קריאת שמע if there is time before sunrise. If not, he covers himself in the water and says it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he went down to immerse: if he can come up, cover himself, and recite before sunrise, he should come up, cover himself, and recite. If not, he should cover himself in the water and recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: someone in the water immersing as morning time is running out for קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal is to say קריאת שמע dressed and out of the water. But the time for the מצוה matters more, so if waiting would make him miss sunrise, he says it while in the water. The water serves as his covering.

keyTerms.meaning: To immerse in water for purity

phrases.english: If he went down to immerse, if he is able to come up
and cover himself and recite
before sunrise arrives,
he should come up, cover himself, and recite;
and if not, he should cover himself in the water and recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָרַד לִטְבּוֹל, אִם יָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say קריאת שמע out of the water if there is time before sunrise; otherwise, say it covered by the water.

steps.title: משנה: Not in foul water, and four אמות from filth
steps.stepSummary: The water used as a cover cannot be foul or flax-soaking water unless fresh water is added. One must stay four אמות away from such water and from צואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not cover himself in foul water or in flax-soaking water until he pours water into it. And how far must he distance himself from them and from feces? Four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the previous rule and then states a general distance rule for saying holy words near something disgusting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the water as a cover only works if the water is not repulsive. Foul-smelling water is treated like filth. The משנה then sets a measure: four אמות away from bad-smelling water and from צואה.

keyTerms.meaning: Water used to soak flax (smells bad)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: (1) shorten תפלה; (2) say שמע before sunrise, in the water if needed; (3) not in foul water, and keep four אמות from filth.

phrases.english: But he may not cover himself in foul water
nor in flax-soaking water,
until he pours water into it.
And how far must he distance himself from them and from feces?
Four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יִתְכַּסֶּה לֹא בַּמַּיִם הָרָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the 'cover in water' rule and adds a distance measure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No covering in foul water unless diluted; keep four אמות from foul water and צואה.

steps.title: ברייתא: Same rule for תפלה, plus reading the תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the משנה's rule about תפלה. It adds that a בעל קרי reading the תורה does not stop to go immerse, but keeps reading quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: If one was standing in prayer and remembered he had a seminal emission, he should not stop but shorten. If one was reading the תורה and remembered he had a seminal emission, he does not stop and go up, but reads quickly and continues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא. It repeats the משנה and then adds a new case about קריאת התורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeat is real. It sets up the new case. With תפלה he shortens. With reading the תורה he does not leave to immerse. He keeps reading, but hurriedly and not in a full clear chant.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion
And goes up / leaves (breaks off from the reading)
Reads hurriedly or haltingly, without full clear diction

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי —
phrases.english: If one was standing in prayer and remembered he had a seminal emission,
he should not stop, but shorten.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה קוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי —
phrases.english: If he was reading the Torah and remembered he had a seminal emission,
he does not stop and leave (the reading),
but rather reads hurriedly and continues.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that echoes the משנה and extends it to reading the תורה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי in middle of reading the תורה keeps reading quickly; he does not leave to immerse.

steps.title: רבי מאיר limits reading the תורה to three פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees. He says a בעל קרי may not read more than three פסוקים in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A person who had a seminal emission is not allowed to read more than three verses in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי מאיר gives a dissenting view about the Torah-reading case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion lets him finish his reading. רבי מאיר allows only the minimum of three פסוקים, which is the smallest amount a reader may read. After that he must stop and let someone else continue.

keyTerms.meaning: Three verses, the minimum for one reader

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
One who had a seminal emission is not permitted
to read in the Torah more than three verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵין בַּעַל קֶרִי רַשַּׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dissents from the first opinion's Torah-reading rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי may read at most three פסוקים.

steps.title: ברייתא: Walk forward past צואה seen during תפלה
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches that if someone sees צואה in front of him during תפלה, he walks forward until it is four אמות behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: If one was standing in prayer and saw feces in front of him, he walks forward until he has placed it four אמות behind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that applies the four-אמות rule from the משנה to תפלה. This sets up a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the distance of four אמות. This ברייתא says how to reach it: walk forward past the צואה until it is four אמות behind you.

phrases.english: Another baraita taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְרָאָה צוֹאָה כְּנֶגְדּוֹ —
phrases.english: If one was standing in prayer and saw feces in front of him,
he walks forward
until he places it four cubits behind him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְרָאָה צוֹאָה כְּנֶגְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the משנה's four-אמות rule, applied to תפלה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When seeing צואה during תפלה, walk forward until it is four אמות behind.

steps.title: Contradiction: another source says to the side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from another ברייתא that says moving four אמות to the side is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in another ברייתא: to the side!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two ברייתות seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא requires walking forward so the צואה is behind. Another allows moving four אמות sideways. Both cannot seem right, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But was it not taught' — introduces a contradicting ברייתא

phrases.english: But it was taught: to the side!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא לִצְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 23 using a contradicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא requiring one to walk forward past the צואה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says moving four אמות to the side is enough, so walking forward seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Resolution: forward when possible, sideways when not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that walking forward applies when possible. Moving to the side applies when walking forward is not possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: this one is where it is possible, and that one is where it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking forward is the preferred way, so you keep facing the same direction. If something blocks you from moving forward, stepping four אמות to the side is acceptable. The two sources do not disagree; they describe different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult' — opens a resolution

steps.whatToRemember: Seeing צואה during תפלה: walk forward until it is four אמות behind you. If that is impossible, move four אמות to the side.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where it is possible (to go forward),
that one is where it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא, דְּאֶפְשָׁר, הָא, דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly disagree about which direction is required.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forward is required when possible; sideways is enough only when forward is impossible.

steps.title: A prayer remains valid despite the mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that someone who finds צואה where he prayed has done wrong, but his תפלה still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone was praying and found feces in his place, רבה said: Although he sinned, his prayer is a valid prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces רבה’s ruling about צואה found where a person prayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה separates the person’s mistake from the status of the תפלה. The mistake does not, in his view, make the תפלה invalid.

phrases.english: He was praying and found feces in his place,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא —
phrases.english: Rabba said: Although he sinned—
his prayer is a valid prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving how to move away from צואה seen during תפלה, the גמרא turns to צואה discovered in the place where someone prayed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Despite the person’s wrongdoing, the תפלה counts.

steps.title: A verse challenges the prayer’s validity
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רבה with a verse that calls a wicked person’s offering an abomination.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected to him: But does it not say, “The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination”?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רבה’s claim that this תפלה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes an act of worship as unacceptable. רבא asks how רבה can call this תפלה valid despite the wrongdoing connected to it.

phrases.english: Rava challenged him: But does it not say:
“The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination”!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה’s ruling that the תפלה remains valid.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה’s ruling that the תפלה counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse calls a wrongdoing-linked act of worship an abomination, which conflicts with treating this תפלה as valid.

steps.title: The prayer is unacceptable
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the opposite ruling: although the person prayed, his תפלה is an abomination.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Since he sinned, although he prayed, his prayer is an abomination.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states his ruling after challenging רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the wrongdoing leaves the תפלה valid. רבא says it changes the outcome: the תפלה is unacceptable.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: Since he sinned,
although he prayed—
his prayer is an abomination.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הוֹאִיל וְחָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the ruling that follows from רבא’s challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא rejects the validity of this תפלה and calls it an abomination.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה says the תפלה counts despite the mistake; רבא says it is unacceptable.

steps.title: Stop praying until the urine ceases
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if urine flows onto someone’s knees during תפלה, he stops until it ceases and then resumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone was standing in prayer and urine was flowing onto his knees, he stops until the urine ceases, and then resumes praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case with a ברייתא about an interruption during תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the previous case, the problem arises while the person is still praying. The ברייתא tells him to stop and resume, but does not yet specify where in the תפלה to resume.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: He was standing in prayer
and urine was flowing onto his knees—
he stops until the urine ceases
and resumes praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a completed תפלה whose place was found unfit to a problem that interrupts תפלה in progress.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stop until the urine ceases, then resume praying.

steps.title: Where does he resume?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which point in the תפלה the person returns to.
steps.simpleTranslation: To where does he return?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a detail the ברייתא left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: “Resume” could mean start the תפלה again or continue from the stopping point. The question asks which one the ברייתא requires.

phrases.english: To where does he return?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהֵיכָן חוֹזֵר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא means by resuming תפלה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the person resumes at the beginning or at the point where he stopped.

steps.title: Two views on where to resume
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree: one says to start over, and the other says to continue from where the person stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב המנונא: one said he returns to the beginning, and one said to the place where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents two answers to its question, without saying which רב gave which answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views accept that the person stops until the urine ceases. Their disagreement is only about whether the earlier part of the תפלה still counts toward this תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: to the point where he stopped

phrases.english: Rav Hisda and Rav Hamnuna,
one said he returns to the beginning,
and one said: to the place where he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the two positions on the question just asked.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a disagreement: return to the beginning or continue from the stopping point.

steps.title: What is behind the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to propose what the two views may disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that they disagree about this:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up an explanation for the disagreement. The proposed explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two practical answers are already clear. Now the גמרא turns to the reason for the difference between them; this line does not yet state that reason.

phrases.english: Let us say that they disagree about this:

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to examine what accounts for the two views.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying point on which the two views disagree.
